Benchmark Screening Methods: Wall Time and Memory

Source: R/63-BenchMemory.R
BenchMemory.Rd

Runs every screening method listed in a BenchMemoryConfig on the same data and measures its wall time and memory footprint with bench::mark().

Usage

BenchMemory(obj, ...)

# S3 method for class '`SigBridgeR::BenchMemoryConfig`'
BenchMemory(obj, ..., verbose = getFuncOption("verbose"))

# Default S3 method
BenchMemory(obj, ...)

Arguments

obj

An object of class BenchMemoryConfig

...

Additional arguments passed to methods. Currently unused.

verbose

logical. Whether to report progress. Default: getFuncOption("verbose").

Value

A data.table with one row per screening method per round. Each row contains the bench::mark() columns (min, median, itr/sec, mem_alloc, n_itr, n_gc, total_time, ...), with expression replaced by the method name, plus method_name, round, position, status, error, mem_peak_mb, rss_peak_mb and elapsed. Successful measurements have status = "ok"; failed or timed-out measurements are kept with status set to "error" or "timeout" and NA memory metrics, while their benchmark columns are filled with NA.

Details

The benchmark is organised in rounds. Within a round every method is screened once, and the round order is shuffled by default so that cold-cache, lazy-loading and package-level caching effects are spread across methods instead of always penalising the first one. One row is returned per method per round; summaries across rounds are left to the caller.

Each measurement runs in its own background R process (callr::r_bg()) with its own copies of the inputs, staged in a temporary directory with qs2. A child process therefore cannot leak package-level caches, loaded Python runtimes or large result objects into the next measurement. The child is always terminated on exit so it cannot outlive the call, and timeout_sec bounds the wall time of a single method in a single round.

Three memory numbers are reported because they mean different things:

  • mem_alloc - bytes allocated during the run (allocation churn, from bench::mark()).

  • mem_peak_mb - peak R heap high-water mark, from gc(reset = TRUE).

  • rss_peak_mb - peak process resident set size, recorded only when measure_rss = TRUE (Linux only).

Before the benchmark starts, bench_probe_resources() collects a machine resource summary. Set probe_resources = FALSE in the bench_config controls (see BenchMemoryConfigSet()) to skip this probe, for example when the workspace is large and the probe's full gc() would add noticeable startup time.

Benchmark controls (bench_config)

  • rounds (3L): number of rounds; every method is screened once per round.

  • probe_resources (TRUE): whether to call bench_probe_resources() before staging the inputs. Set to FALSE to skip the probe and its full gc().

  • min_iterations, max_iterations (1L, 1L): iteration bounds passed to bench::mark().

  • order ("random"): "random" shuffles methods within each round using seed plus the round number; "fixed" keeps the given order.

  • seed (getFuncOption("seed")): base seed for shuffling and for each measurement child.

  • memory, filter_gc, check, min_time, relative, time_unit: forwarded to bench::mark().

  • measure_rss (FALSE): also record peak process RSS (Linux only).

  • on_failure ("skip"): "skip" records the failure and continues, "stop" aborts the whole benchmark.

  • set_threads (1L): number of threads the child process is pinned to.

  • timeout_sec (10800L): maximum wall-clock seconds for one method in one round; use Inf to disable the limit.

See also

BenchMemoryConfig(), BenchMemoryConfigSet(), bench::mark()

Other Benchmark: BenchAcc(), BenchGSEA(), BenchGeneScore()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
config <- BenchMemoryConfig(
  matched_bulk = bulk,
  sc_data = sc,
  phenotype = pheno,
  screen_method = c("scPP", "scPAS", "LP_SGL"),
  method_param = MethodParamSet(list(
    scPP_param = list(Log2FC_cutoff = 0.585),
    scPAS_param = list(permutation_times = 500)
  )),
  bench_config = list(rounds = 3L, timeout_sec = 1800)
)
res <- BenchMemory(config)
res
res[status == "ok", .(median_sec = median(median)), by = method_name]
} # }
